The `typeof`/`!== null` guard only narrows the type for WeakSet.has. The set holds nothing but Error objects (noteFailureAfterSatisfied is called with a resolver's normalized Error), and WeakSet.has returns false for a primitive, a function or null without throwing. So `(a || b) && has(error)` gives the same `satisfied` as `a && b && has(error)` for every input. Same reasoning as the 357:7 and 358:7 ConditionalExpression entries. Applied by hand, the whole conformance:local suite at MUTATION_LAYER=L3 passes.
